newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan scraps emperor's birthday events over crisis.
newsitem.headline: Japan scraps emperor's birthday events over crisis.

text.p: Japan said on Thursday it would cancel all formal events marking Emperor Akihito's birthday next week due to the hostage crisis in the Japanese ambassador's residence in Peru.
"We have decided to cancel all functions celebrating the Emperor's birthday on December 23," a spokesman for the Imperial Household Agency said in a statement.
"His Majesty the Emperor is concerned about the incident."
The palace decision was made after a request by Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto, the spokesman said.

Leftist guerrillas stormed the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima during a party there on Tuesday in honour of Akihito's 63rd birthday, taking hundreds of people hostage, including diplomats, dignitaries and Peruvian government ministers.

The guerrillas freed a number of hostages on Wednesday and government officials were negotiating with the rebels to try to resolve the crisis. Japanese Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda left for Lima on Thursday to try to help win the release of the around 480 hostages remaining in the compound.
The emperor had been due to hold a party on his birthday, to which diplomats, politicians and celebrities were invited.
He was also scheduled to speak from a glassed-in balcony at the palace to well-wishers. The emperor's birthday is a public holiday in Japan.
Akihito ascended the Chrysanthemum Throne in January 1989 after the death of his father, Hirohito.

The guerrillas, calling for the release of jailed comrades, have called on Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori to personally negotiate with them and have threatened to kill their captives if their demands are not met.
Guerrilla spokesmen in Peru have said the rebels attacked the Japanese ambassador's home in protest at Tokyo's support for Fujimori, the son of Japanese immigrants, and his economic policies.
Governments around the world have urged Peru to do everything in its power to protect the hostages and not use force to flush out the rebels.
